hook_text: TB, cholera, HIV and malaria are four completely different germs. Each one uses a different door to get into you, and each door has a lock.
clip_script: A germ is stuck unless it can get from one person to the next, so every disease has a favourite door. TB is a bacterium that uses the air door: one cough fills a taxi with droplets. Lock it with an elbow over your cough, open windows, and six months of tablets that you finish. Cholera is a bacterium that uses the water door: sewage gets into drinking water and causes diarrhoea so severe it can kill in hours. Lock it with soap, boiled water, and a drink of clean water, six teaspoons of sugar and half a teaspoon of salt. HIV is a virus that uses the blood door: blood and body fluids only, never hugs, cups or mosquitoes. Lock it with condoms, never sharing needles, and knowing your status; daily tablets keep it under control. Malaria is a tiny protist that uses the bite door: a mosquito at night. Lock it with a net. Know the door, use the lock.
visual_style: Four whiteboard doors labelled air, water, blood and bite, each with a germ icon behind it; a padlock snaps onto each door as its prevention is named.
mood: Clear, calm and empowering rather than frightening.
pacing: Steady rhythm of four doors, one lock each, with a crisp final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and match every prevention method to the door it locks.
